description: This file defines an API for managing a set of object IDs (oids) using a hash-based data structure, including functions for initialization, insertion, removal, comparison, parsing from files, and iteration.

methods.name: oidset_init
methods.description: Initializes the oidset structure, optionally preallocating memory based on the provided initial size.

methods.name: oidset_contains
methods.description: Checks if the specified oid exists within the set.

methods.name: oidset_equal
methods.description: Compares two oidsets for equality, checking if they contain the same set of OIDs.

methods.name: oidset_insert
methods.description: Inserts a copy of the given oid into the set, returning 1 if it was already present, 0 if newly inserted.

methods.name: oidset_insert_from_set
methods.description: Inserts all OIDs from a source set into a destination set.

methods.name: oidset_remove
methods.description: Removes the specified oid from the set, returning 1 if it was present.

methods.name: int oidset_size(const struct oidset * set)
methods.description: Returns the number of OIDs currently stored in the set.

methods.name: oidset_clear
methods.description: Removes all entries from the set and frees associated resources.

methods.name: oidset_parse_file
methods.description: Reads OIDs from a file, adding them to the set, with support for comments and whitespace handling.

methods.name: oidset_parse_file_carefully
methods.description: Similar to oidset_parse_file, but allows for a callback to handle custom parsing or peeling of OIDs.

methods.name: void oidset_iter_init(const struct oidset * set,struct oidset_iter * iter)
methods.description: Initializes an iterator for traversing the set.

methods.name: struct:object_id * oidset_iter_next(struct oidset_iter * iter)
methods.description: Advances the iterator and returns the next OID.

methods.name: struct:object_id * oidset_iter_first(struct oidset * set,struct oidset_iter * iter)
methods.description: Resets the iterator and returns the first OID in the set.
